question: Rays coming from the sun are refracted by the atmosphere. Due to this, the apparent sunrise is about ________ the actual sunrise.
solution:
The correct answer is __**2 minutes before**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The apparent sunrise occurs about **2 minutes before** the actual sunrise due to atmospheric refraction.
 
• Atmospheric refraction bends the light rays coming from the sun, making the sun appear above the horizon when it is still below it.
 
• This phenomenon causes the sun to be seen earlier than its actual geometric position relative to the horizon.
 
• Similarly, during sunset, the sun is visible for about 2 minutes after it has actually set below the horizon.
 
• This effect is more pronounced at higher latitudes and during certain times of the year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atmospheric refraction** is the bending of light as it passes through the Earth's atmosphere, which has varying density layers.
 
• This bending of light causes celestial objects to appear higher in the sky than their actual geometric position.
 
• The phenomenon is also responsible for the apparent flattening of the sun's disk near the horizon.
 
• Understanding atmospheric refraction is crucial for accurate astronomical observations and navigation.
